prs.title: fix: don't throw on import when window.screen is unavailable
prs.author: jkugsiya
prs.body:
Closes #10760

Importing `react-aria` in a React Native Jest environment (jest-expo) throws `TypeError: Reflect.has called on non-object`. React Native's Jest preset sets `window` to the global object, which has no `screen`. The test-only orientation shim added in 3.53.0 then calls `Reflect.has(window.screen, 'orientation')` on `undefined`.

This adds a `window.screen != null` check to the shim's condition, one level above the check from #10743. As discussed on the issue, it also covers runtimes like Deno that have no `window.screen`. No other code runs at import there, since the global event setup only runs when `document` exists.

No unit test: the shared Jest setup needs jsdom's `window`, so a React Native-like environment can't run in this suite. I checked it locally with a `node` environment test that sets `window` to the global object and skips the shared setup. It fails with the reported `TypeError` before this change and passes after.

prs.title: fix: report every user caret move through TokenField onChange
prs.author: UditDewan
prs.body:
Closes #10764

`setTokenFieldSelection` set `root[isProgrammaticSelectionChange]` before the "only set selection if it has changed" check. After a user caret move, the `selectionchange` handler stores the new range, the layout effect calls `setTokenFieldSelection` with the position the browser already has, and `setBaseAndExtent` is skipped. No `selectionchange` follows to consume the flag, so `useSelectionChange` discards the next real one. That's why `onChange` only fired for every second caret move and `value.selectedRange` fell one step behind the DOM selection.

The fix only sets the flag when `setBaseAndExtent` is actually called. When `fireEvent` is true and the selection is unchanged, any pending flag is left alone, which is correct since its `selectionchange` is still on the way.

The WebKit-only Shift+ArrowLeft-across-tokens observation in the issue is not addressed here; the issue notes it still happens with this change applied, so it looks like a separate bug.

#10765 by @maricastroc reached the same fix independently and was closed in favor of this PR. I briefly swapped in its test, which also crosses a token with ArrowLeft, but that step fails in WebKit on CI (likely the separate WebKit behavior above), so I reverted to the plain-text test.

prs.title: fix: Fix style macro build in ESM
prs.author: devongovett
prs.body: The ESM build of style macro current throws when run with `Error evaluating macro: $kLxT8$propertiesmjs1 is not defined`. It looks like the [current build](https://app.unpkg.com/@react-spectrum/s2@1.8.1/files/style/dist/style-macro.mjs) defines `$kLxT8$propertiesmjs2` but not `$kLxT8$propertiesmjs1` or `$kLxT8$propertiesmjs`. Probably a bug in Parcel v2 which builds this. A workaround is to use a default import rather than namespace.
